title: Iteration releasability
description: Assess each integrated increment against its accepted Definition of Done, apply requested scoped fixes, verify artifacts, and report ready, blocked, or unverified.
intent: Assess whether the named product increment remains usable and releasable for its target after the iteration. Reuse accepted gates and current evidence. Review alone authorizes no source/tracker changes or publication; implement only requested remediation, then recheck the final snapshot.

assignments.task: Identify accepted goals, integrated product boundaries, named target, revision/dirty-state/artifact identity, Definition of Done basis, applicable required gates, existing evidence, and requested review/remediation scope.
Map accepted delivered/partial/deferred requirements and dependencies without changing trackers.
assignments.when: Multiple work items, milestone completeness, scope drift, or accepted exception status need clarification.

assignments.task: Clarify accepted user outcomes and testable acceptance criteria; distinguish proposals from commitments.
assignments.when: Product acceptance decisions are material and this role is installed.

assignments.task: Assess relevant integration, rollout order, compatibility, or consequential boundary constraints before requested repairs.
assignments.when: The increment changes consequential contracts, persistence, or system boundaries.

assignments.task: Map affected complete journeys, context preservation, alternatives, and recovery against the accepted scope.
assignments.when: End-to-end user behavior or partially exposed flows are material to the increment.

assignments.task: Apply only requested scoped Definition of Done/iteration fixes, reproduce defects, preserve unrelated work and baseline failures, and run applicable checks. Do not weaken criteria, change rollout scope, or publish.
assignments.when: The user requests remediation or implementation of the identified increment; readiness assessment alone does not satisfy this condition.

assignments.task: Check completed acceptance behavior, existing critical regressions, integration/state transitions, and actual check results for the stable snapshot.
Assess applicable changed trust/data boundaries and required security gates.
assignments.when: Security/privacy boundaries or an accepted security gate are affected.

assignments.task: Independently walk through meaningful existing/new task paths and recovery using actual available evidence.
assignments.when: The increment changes user-facing task behavior or requires a usability gate.

assignments.task: Assess affected semantics, keyboard/focus, forms, reflow, and actual assistive/automation evidence against accepted criteria.
assignments.when: Meaningful access behavior or an accepted accessibility gate is affected.

assignments.task: Review affected completed UI/component/theme states against the project system and accepted behavior.
assignments.when: Visual/system UI changes or a relevant design gate are part of the increment.

assignments.task: Check required performance budgets with comparable actual evidence; avoid unrequested load or new benchmark programs.
assignments.when: The increment affects a documented hot path/budget or makes a material performance claim.

assignments.task: Check material public/calculation/provenance claims and supporting check/source identities.
assignments.when: The increment includes consequential quantitative, factual, provenance, or improvement claims.

assignments.task: Verify applicable built artifact identity, isolated consumer installation/startup/smoke behavior, configuration, compatibility, migrations, and recovery evidence. Reuse current retained checks where valid; do not bump versions, tag, publish, deploy, or perform destructive recovery.
assignments.when: The accepted target requires artifact/consumer/startup or operational gates; missing access remains unverified rather than a skipped requirement.

assignments.task: Reconcile completed specialist/artifact results against required gates for the final snapshot. Report ready, blocked, or unverified, accepted exceptions, stale/missing evidence, and next actions. Requested corrections return to the single writer and affected checks rerun before a fresh verdict.

completion: The named increment, integrated product boundary, Definition of Done basis, target, and reviewed snapshot are explicit.
Requested fixes precede dependent independent checks; artifact/consumer evidence and specialist results precede the final verdict.
Ready requires all applicable required gates to pass with current evidence; confirmed required failure means blocked, otherwise required unknowns mean unverified.
Existing critical behavior and exposed new flows remain part of acceptance; unfinished work is isolated only with supporting evidence.
Accepted exceptions have an actual policy/authorization basis; criteria are not lowered to hide failures.
Review-only scope preserves source/trackers, and readiness neither publishes nor claims automatic CI/host enforcement.
